description:
FOUND s488b (Opus), by the probe #1841 (c) asked for -- the first MEASUREMENT of
a hole the runtime already names in prose ("WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT COVER, said
out loud rather than assumed: a dependency that MOVES -- a new `-I` shadowing a
shim, so the same name now resolves to a DIFFERENT file -- is not detected here;
only 'did not resolve, now does' is", cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the manifest section).

REPRODUCER (kept: scratch/s488b/probes/inc-move.pl in the s488b worktree; it is
~40 lines and self-contained).  Two `-I` directories, each with a `B2.pm` whose
`zap` differs only in an EMPTY PROTOTYPE -- a PARSE fact, so it changes the
EMISSION of anything that uses it: with the prototype `zap + 1` is `zap()+1`,
without it `zap(+1)` and zap sees an argument.

  d1/B2.pm:  sub zap () { return 7 + (@_ ? 100 : 0) }   # exported
  d2/B2.pm:  sub zap    { return 7 + (@_ ? 100 : 0) }
  shared/A3.pm:  package A3; use B2; sub go { return zap + 1 }
  shared/prog.pl: use A3; print A3::go();

Three passes against ONE cache dir, `-I shared -I d1`, then `-I shared -I d2`,
then `-I shared -I d1`:

  perl:   8 / 107 / 8
  pcl:    8 /   8 / 8      <-- pass 2 DIVERGES

WHY: A3's key is A3's own absolute path (plus the generation and the compiler
fingerprint) -- the include path is not in it -- and its manifest records
`dep mod B2 <md5> /d1/B2.pm`.  On pass 2 that file still exists and still
hashes to what was read, so `%p-manifest-at` says VALID and the cached
emission, which encodes d1's prototype, is served.  `missing` covers only
absent -> present (#1284).

NOT the script side: the same probe run with the program itself reading B2
agrees with perl on all three passes, because a main script is transpiled on
every run today.  That is exactly why task #1841's script cache puts the `-I`
list in its key -- without it, caching the script would GIVE scripts this bug.

FIX SHAPE (not done here): re-RESOLVE each recorded dependency NAME at load and
compare the path, not only the hash.  The transpiler's own memo already does
it and its POD says why -- Pl/ProtoCache.pm: "the entry records each dependency
it resolved -- module name, the path it resolved to under the inc_paths in
force, mtime and size -- and a hit re-resolves each name and re-stats it.  That
covers both 'a dependency changed' and 'a dependency now resolves somewhere
else' (a dist's t/lib shadowing a shipped shim)".  The manifest already carries
the NAME beside the path (`dep<TAB>kind<TAB>NAME<TAB>class<TAB>sha<TAB>PATH`),
and the resolver is at hand (`p-find-module-in-inc`, the ONE resolver, over a
superset of the child's list since #1284) -- so the change is one more clause
in `%p-manifest-at`'s verdict, beside the `missing` re-check it already runs:
for each `dep` of kind `mod`, `(p-find-module-in-inc (p-module-to-path NAME))`
must answer the recorded PATH.  Cost: one probe-file per dependency per module
load, on the same order as the MD5 it already pays.

MEASURE BEFORE SHIPPING: the shim `lib/` is on `Pl::Parser`'s inc_paths FIRST
but is deliberately NOT on the child perl's `-I` (%p-shim-lib-dir-p), so the
runtime-side resolver and the transpile-side resolver disagree for exactly the
shimmed core modules (Errno, Config, POSIX, Carp...).  A naive path comparison
would call every shim dependency STALE on every run -- an endless
re-transpile.  So the clause needs the same exclusion the child's `-I` list
uses, and the acceptance bar is a full sweep with the fasl/transpile counts
unchanged, not just the reproducer above going green.

Related: #1261 (the manifest), #1284 (`missing` re-check), #1841 (the script
cache, which keys the include path for this reason), #560 (ProtoCache).

=== THE SCRIPT CACHE NOW INHERITS THE UNCHANGED-SEARCH-PATH HALF (s488b, same session) ===

#1841 shipped, so the "NOT the script side" paragraph above needs one
qualification, stated so nobody reads this task as script-safe:

  * the half the probe measured -- the `-I` LIST CHANGES -- is closed for a
    script by #1841's key (the -I list, the cwd and PERL5LIB are in it), so
    that probe stays green after #1841;
  * the half this task's own FIX SHAPE addresses -- a dependency whose NAME
    resolves ELSEWHERE while the search path is UNCHANGED (a new file created
    earlier on an already-present -I directory, a shim shadowed by a dist's
    t/lib appearing later) -- is NOT closed by any key, because nothing in it
    moves.  A main script was immune to it until #1841 only because it was
    re-transpiled on every run; now its entry survives exactly as a module's
    does.

So this task's prize grew: it is the one fix that covers both populations,
and after #1841 it is the only remaining resolution hole in either.

=== MEASURED s488b: #1841 MAKES THE SECOND HALF A NEW REGRESSION FOR A SCRIPT ===

The note above said the unchanged-search-path half "is NOT closed by any key".
It is worse than that, and it was measured rather than reasoned:
**pre-#1841 PCL answered CORRECTLY and post-#1841 it does not**, because the
script was re-transpiled on every run.

REPRODUCER (kept: scratch/s488b/probes/shadow-later.pl, and shadow-later2.pl
which takes the tree in $PCL_TREE).  `-I d1 -I d2` on ALL THREE passes -- the
search path never changes.  Pass 1: only `d2/B4.pm` exists, `zap` with NO
prototype, so `zap + 1` is `zap(+1)` = 107.  Then `d1/B4.pm` is CREATED --
earlier on the same, unchanged -I list -- with `sub zap ()`, an empty
prototype, so perl now parses `zap + 1` as `zap() + 1` = 8.

  pass                                    perl   PCL @ f26282db   PCL @ #1841
  1  only d2/B4.pm (no prototype)          107        107             107
  2  d1/B4.pm created (with prototype)       8          8            *107*
  3  same again                              8          8            *107*

One entry in <cache>/scripts/.  Nothing in its KEY moved (same path, same
path-as-given, same cwd, same -I list, same PERL5LIB, same generation, same
fingerprint), and the manifest's `dep mod B4 <md5> /d2/B4.pm` still exists and
still hashes to what was read -- so `%p-manifest-at` says VALID and yesterday's
parse is served.  `missing` does not fire: B4 DID resolve.

SO THIS TASK IS NOW A REGRESSION OWNER, not only a latent-hole owner, and it
is the deciding input to the USER's DEFAULT-ON-vs-OPT-IN question on #1841:
default-on ships this shape.  The fix shape above (re-resolve each recorded
`dep mod NAME` and require the recorded PATH) closes it for both populations
at once -- and the MEASURE-BEFORE-SHIPPING paragraph above is exactly why it
was not attempted at the end of the s488b batch: for a SCRIPT the child's `-I`
list is known exactly (`pcl` hands it to `p-run-script-cached`), so a
script-only clause might dodge the shim-lib disagreement, but that is a design
call with a full-sweep acceptance bar, not a filler.

=== THE REPRODUCER, EMBEDDED (the s488b worktree is deleted at merge) ===

#!/usr/bin/env perl
# Does a SCRIPT cache entry survive a dependency whose NAME starts resolving to
# a DIFFERENT file while the search path is UNCHANGED?  (#1860's second half,
# which a script entry inherits since #1841 -- before it, a script was
# re-transpiled every run and always saw the new file.)
#
# Shape: -I d1 -I d2 for all three passes.  Pass 1: only d2/B4.pm exists.
# Then d1/B4.pm is CREATED (earlier on the same, unchanged -I list) with a
# different PROTOTYPE, which is a parse fact.  perl must switch; PCL's entry
# key cannot notice (nothing in it moved) and the manifest records d2/B4.pm,
# which still exists and still hashes as read.
use strict; use warnings;
use File::Temp qw(tempdir);
use File::Path qw(make_path);
use Cwd qw(abs_path);

my $root  = abs_path("$0/../../../..");           # the worktree
my $dir   = tempdir(CLEANUP => 1);
my $cache = "$dir/cache";
make_path("$dir/d1", "$dir/d2");

# with an empty prototype:  zap + 1  ==  zap() + 1  == 7 + 1   = 8
# without:                  zap + 1  ==  zap(+1)    == 7 + 100 = 107
my $PROTO = "package B4;\nuse Exporter 'import';\nour \@EXPORT = ('zap');\n"
          . "sub zap () { return 7 + (\@_ ? 100 : 0) }\n1;\n";
my $PLAIN = "package B4;\nuse Exporter 'import';\nour \@EXPORT = ('zap');\n"
          . "sub zap    { return 7 + (\@_ ? 100 : 0) }\n1;\n";

open my $h, '>', "$dir/d2/B4.pm" or die; print $h $PLAIN; close $h;   # no proto
open $h, '>', "$dir/prog.pl" or die;
print $h "use B4;\nprint zap + 1, \"\\n\";\n"; close $h;
my $spec = "-I $dir/d1 -I $dir/d2";

sub run {
  my ($cmd) = @_;
  my $out = qx{$cmd 2>/dev/null};
  $out =~ s/\s+\z//;
  return $out;
}
my $pcl  = "PCL_CACHE_DIR='$cache' $root/pcl $spec '$dir/prog.pl'";
my $perl = "perl $spec '$dir/prog.pl'";

printf "pass 1 (only d2/B4.pm, NO prototype):  perl=%s  pcl=%s   (expect 107/107)\n",
       run($perl), run($pcl);

# create d1/B4.pm WITH the prototype -- earlier on the SAME -I list
open $h, '>', "$dir/d1/B4.pm" or die; print $h $PROTO; close $h;

printf "pass 2 (d1/B4.pm created, WITH proto): perl=%s  pcl=%s   (perl must be 8)\n",
       run($perl), run($pcl);
printf "pass 3 (same again):                   perl=%s  pcl=%s\n",
       run($perl), run($pcl);
print "entries in scripts/: ", scalar(() = glob("$cache/scripts/*.lisp")), "\n";

=== DONE (s490a, 2026-09-18, member 1) ===

THE DESIGN THAT SHIPPED is the ruled one, not this task's original "re-resolve
with p-find-module-in-inc and compare": the manifest is now SELF-DESCRIBING,
because the runtime cannot ask the transpiler's question.  The transpiler's
list is [the file's own `use lib` dirs, PCL's shim lib/, the child's @INC] â
not @INC â and emulating it from the runtime is the endless-re-transpile trap
this task's own MEASURE-BEFORE-SHIPPING paragraph warned about.

WHAT THE TRANSPILE SIDE RECORDS, from the ONE resolver (`_find_module_file`),
per resolved `mod` dependency:
    resolve<TAB>mod<TAB>NAME<TAB>head|base
    tried<TAB>mod<TAB>NAME<TAB>/abs/dir        (one per dir probed BEFORE the hit)
`head` = at or before `$_pcl_lib_dir` (a `use lib` dir or the shim), `base` =
the child perl's @INC part.  Directories are rel2abs'd (NEVER abs_path: a
`use lib 't/lib'` that does not exist yet is exactly the directory R1 watches,
and abs_path answers undef for it); a non-string inc_paths entry is skipped.

THE FOUR PATHS A `mod` DEP REACHES THE MANIFEST, all covered: the fresh walk
(`note_dep`), the L1 memo hit (`_note_module_dep`), the L2 `Pl::ProtoCache`
hit, and `note_deps` replaying a frame.  The facts ride as a 6th field on the
dep record; `note_deps` re-reads them from `%RESOLVED` (keyed "name\0path")
rather than copying, because on the L2 path `load()` has just re-resolved every
`mod` name under THIS process's inc_paths â so they are never stored in the
proto-cache JSON and its arity does not move (`store` strips to five fields).

THE RUNTIME CLAUSES (`%p-dep-shadowed-p` / `%p-dep-moved-p`, dispatched by
`%p-mod-dep-resolves-as-recorded-p`, memoised per (dir, rel-path) in
`*p-inc-probe-cache*`):
  R1  no recorded `tried` directory holds the dependency's file NOW.
  R2  for a BASE hit only, the first directory a child transpile would search
      now (`%p-child-inc-dirs` â factored out of `%p-transpile-inc-args`, so
      the -I builder and R2 share ONE definition) that holds the file must be
      the recorded file, compared as truenames.  Nothing found = no evidence.
  A `dep mod` line with no `resolve` line makes the manifest INVALID (rule 12).

DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF, with its reason: the brief said R2 walks
`p-find-module-in-inc`'s list.  For a SCRIPT that list is the SEED (`$srcdir`,
`.`, â¦) which the child does NOT get as `-I` (`pcl` hands it
`inc_dirs_for_transpile`), so a module beside the script would be a permanent
false stale â and R2 buys a script nothing, its key already carrying the -I
list, the cwd and PERL5LIB.  So R2 is a keyword `:check-move` on the verdict,
passed T by the MODULE layer and explicitly NIL by the script and eval layers
(never a silent skip), and it walks the CHILD's -I list.  R1 runs everywhere.

MEASURED.  Fable's review probe p1860.pl: all 25 rows agree with perl,
including the three shadow scenarios AND the six breaking cases.  THE
ACCEPTANCE MEASUREMENT (a needless re-transpile still prints the right answer,
so "0 new" proves nothing): nine `pcl` runs over modules/scripts/evals against
ONE fresh PCL_CACHE_DIR, twice, counting entries the second run REPLACED, by
INODE.  base+member-0: 0 / 50 modules, 0 / 18 scripts, 0 / 178 evals.  This
tree: 0 / 0 / 0 with the same entry counts â EQUAL, as the bar requires.
WARM-START COST, interleaved A/B (the first, block-form run compared the box's
load as much as the trees): one-module script base 0.0467 best / 0.0511 median
vs tree 0.0466 / 0.0493; `use Moo` + `has` base 4.991 / 5.114 vs tree 4.887 /
5.028.  No measurable cost, both inside the brief's 1 ms / 2 % bars.

GUARD: Pl/t/cache-validity-01.t, 26 rows, 17.6 s.  Half of them are the OTHER
direction (a shim dependency, a `use lib` dependency, a file created LATER on
the path than the hit â all HITs, asserted by INODE, never by timing).
Inverse-verified on ab4da8b4+member-0: 7 rows fail there.  The fixtures are
BACKDATED â without that, a stale entry answers correctly about half the time
because the entry is not strictly newer than a source written in the same
second, which made the inverse verification itself flaky.
subject: SILENT WRONG, MEASURED (s488b): a cached entry survives a change in WHICH FILE a dependency NAME resolves to -- the manifest re-hashes the OLD path, which still exists.  Two halves: a -I LIST change (closed for a SCRIPT by #1841's key, still open for a MODULE) and a file CREATED earlier on an UNCHANGED search path (open for both, and a NEW REGRESSION for a main script since #1841 -- pre-#1841 PCL answered as perl because the script was re-transpiled every run)
